V09-C03: mean-variance optimization and allocation
Release: v09-c03-allocation-1

Purpose and files
-----------------
This is an original, small synthetic teaching fixture. It is not a financial
recommendation, observed market dataset, empirical backtest or general-purpose
portfolio engine. Keep these four files together:
  v09-c03-inputs.json
  v09-c03-analysis.py
  v09-c03-output.json
  v09-c03-README.txt
The separate v09-c03-manifest.json identifies their byte sizes and SHA256 hashes.
The manuscript's focused checker lives in scripts/check_v09_c03.py in the source
edition; it independently checks the mathematics, boundaries and this manifest.

Run using standard-library Python 3, from any working directory:
  python3 /path/to/v09-c03-analysis.py
  python3 /path/to/v09-c03-analysis.py --input /path/to/v09-c03-inputs.json
  python3 /path/to/v09-c03-analysis.py --output /path/to/new-output.json
The default input is beside the script, not relative to your current directory.
Without --output, the command emits one JSON object. Importing emits nothing;
run(inputs) returns JSON-compatible data without writing or printing. run() loads
the adjacent supplied input. The output file is the full preserved baseline.

Units, dates and rights
----------------------
All returns are one-year simple total returns, in decimal units and a common CU
currency; variance is in squared decimal-return units. All weights are exposures
per unit of beginning wealth. There is one date-0 trade and date-1 realization,
with no tax, fees, intermediate cash distributions or rebalancing.

The unconstrained three-asset cases permit real signed risky weights and an
explicit safe account that can borrow and lend at the same supplied rate. The
GMV and target frontier use only risky assets with weights summing to one. Cash
allocation instead chooses risky exposures x and supplies cash weight 1-sum(x).
The constrained case has three risky assets only, no cash and no shorts. The
two-asset shrinkage comparison is fully invested in its two risky assets, with
shorting allowed; it is not a safe-asset allocation problem.

Physical states and moments
---------------------------
For every law, independent sign factors take -1 and +1 with equal probability.
Returns equal the supplied means plus factor loadings times those signs. The
main law has four factors and sixteen states, each probability 1/16. Its means
are (4%,8%,12%), and covariance is .01*11' + diag(.01,.04,.09).

The forecast-perturbation covariance is separately generated by five factors
and thirty-two states. D has loading .2 on the first factor. E has loadings
(.198,.026,.010,.004,.002). Their variances are .04 and covariance .0396.
Initially both means are .08; the alternate forecast changes only E to .082.
The six-factor audit law has sixty-four states: D shares its first two .1 factor
loadings with E and has two additional independent .1 loadings; E has two other
independent .1 loadings. Thus audit variances are .04, covariance .02 and means
.08 for both assets. The audit law is an explicitly disclosed synthetic truth
for explaining the example. It is not used to fit or choose the forecast rules.

These states are a population construction, not rows observed from a historical
sample. Moments therefore use their stated probabilities, not an n-1 sample
correction. Positive probabilities do not make these market-pricing weights.
All supplied individual asset returns exceed -1. Covariance matrices must be
SPD for the analytic inverse/linear-system calculations; exact LDL pivots check
that stronger condition. A duplicated asset violates it and is rejected rather
than silently handled by an inverse or pseudoinverse. See the chapter's distinct
discussion of true redundancy versus sample-estimation singularity.

What the output reports
-----------------------
1. Exact reconstructed main means/covariance and SPD pivots; frontier A,B,C,Delta.
2. GMV and all supplied equality-target portfolios, including their efficiency
   branch classification. Means below the GMV mean are on the dominated branch.
3. Risky direction Sigma^-1(mu-rf*1), its sum, actual exposures and safe weight.
   A fully invested positive-premium tangency fund is reported only if that sum
   is strictly positive. Zero and negative sums receive explicit statuses and
   a null fund; optimal cash/risky exposures remain available. With q=0, the
   output labels the all-safe optimum rather than dividing by zero.
4. Complete enumeration of the seven nonempty faces of the three-asset simplex.
   Feasible equality-target minimizers are compared with exact variances. An
   impossible long-only target returns status=infeasible, no selected portfolio
   and the feasible mean interval. It is not replaced by a nearest target.
5. Four fully invested two-asset rules: baseline raw; perturbed raw; covariance
   shrinkage; covariance plus mean shrinkage. The covariance target is trace(S)/2
   times identity. The mean target is the cross-sectional average of the input
   forecast means. Each row reports the actual used inputs, fitted moments and
   its evaluation under the SAME separate audit law. Comparing optimized fitted
   objectives across different input models is not a test of performance.

Every rational value is a JSON string, including integer-valued exact results.
Counts are JSON integers. Fields named *_approx contain Python binary floating
square roots or a ratio using one; these are for display, not exact certificates.
The focused checker uses 1e-12 absolute/relative tolerance for those fields and
exact Fraction equality for all rational identities. Strict JSON excludes NaN
and infinity. No randomness, network, dependency installation or CSV inference
is involved; repeated baseline calculations are deterministic.

Documented changes and failures
------------------------------
Use a COPY of the supplied input for changes. Rational strings such as "1/10"
or "0.10" are supported; JSON floating-point numbers and booleans are rejected
as numerical inputs. Positive gamma, safe gross return above zero, exactly the
declared asset/factor dimensions, positive-definite covariances and individual
state simple returns strictly above -1 are required. A target-return equality
with all identical means is permitted only at that common mean.

You may change numeric means/loadings within those domains, gamma, the safe
rate, target list and long-only target. Shrinkage intensities must be in [0,1].
The raw rules require both intensities zero; covariance_shrunk requires alpha>0
and kappa=0; covariance_and_mean_shrunk requires both positive. Keep all four
rules and their named mean sets. Changing a policy label, horizon, return type,
fee/tax assumption, funding/short right, probability or evaluation convention
does not activate an alternate model: contradictory labels are rejected.
The reference output and manuscript refer to the original input only.

Limitations
-----------
The linear systems and face enumeration condition on supplied moments. They do
not estimate forecasts, authenticate rights, calibrate a risk-aversion coefficient
or incorporate transaction costs, margin calls, unequal borrowing rates or
liability risk. Large portfolios need different numerical methods; this fixture
does not scale the seven-face demonstration into a general solver.

Half shrinkage is an authored example, not the fitted Ledoit-Wolf estimator. It
does not implement their constant-correlation target or optimal-intensity formula.
The audit improvement in this constructed population is not evidence of universal
superiority; if the raw forecast were the population, its own optimum would win.
Normal-exponential expected utility is a separate conditional derivation in the
chapter. These bounded sign-factor laws instead stipulate the mean-variance
objective directly. Arithmetic verification is not external human certification,
source authentication, browser QA or a guarantee of future investment outcomes.
